content.summary: The 5-Amino-1MQ research capsule listing shows a 50 mg strength and a 60-capsule bottle. Published cell research uses the compound to study nicotinamide metabolism.
content.overview: 5-Amino-1MQ is short for 5-amino-1-methylquinolinium, a small molecule from a series of methylquinolinium compounds that researchers developed to inhibit the cytosolic enzyme nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). In one laboratory study, the team measured 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNA), a product of the NNMT reaction, in cultured mouse 3T3-L1 fat cells exposed to the compound and found concentration-dependent reductions; in differentiating cells, the compound also reduced lipid accumulation in a concentration-dependent way. In the same study, the overall effect on intracellular S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) was significant, with a significant increase at one of the concentrations tested; intracellular NAD+ trended upward, but the overall comparison for NAD+ was inconclusive. In enzyme assays at the concentrations tested, it showed little or no inhibition of the related methyltransferases DNMT1, PRMT3 and COMT or of the NAD+ salvage enzymes NAMPT and SIRT1, which the authors interpreted as selectivity for NNMT. In diet-induced obese mice fed a high-fat diet, 5-amino-1MQ reduced body weight and white adipose tissue mass, decreased fat-cell size and lowered plasma total cholesterol without changing total food intake. A 2021 study from the same research group reported that, in obese mice switched to a lean diet, adding the compound produced greater body-weight and fat loss and less liver fat than the diet switch alone. These cell and mouse studies did not test a capsule formulation and do not establish effects of this research material in people. The listed presentation is a 60-count bottle of research capsules with a listed strength of 50 mg.
content.purpose: Laboratory study of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase activity.
content.cautions: For nonclinical laboratory research only.

content.summary: BPC-157 is a 15-amino-acid peptide. This research capsule listing shows a strength of 500 mcg and a package of 60 capsules.
content.overview: BPC-157 is a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide (Gly-Glu-Pro-Pro-Pro-Gly-Lys-Pro-Ala-Asp-Asp-Ala-Gly-Leu-Val) whose sequence is a partial sequence of body protection compound, a protein first isolated from human gastric juice. In cultured rat Achilles tendon explants, it accelerated the outgrowth of tendon fibroblasts. In isolated rat tendon fibroblasts, it did not directly change proliferation but improved cell survival under hydrogen peroxide stress, and it increased cell migration and spreading in a concentration-dependent way, with increased phosphorylation of the focal adhesion proteins FAK and paxillin. A published laboratory study then examined growth hormone receptor expression in fibroblasts isolated from rat Achilles tendons, finding that BPC-157 increased that expression and that adding growth hormone then increased proliferation and activated Janus kinase 2 signaling. A 2025 systematic review of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine included 35 preclinical studies and one retrospective clinical report, and reported that it found no clinical safety data in the literature it reviewed. The cell studies above used the peptide itself, not a capsule formulation, and human use falls outside this listing's research scope. This BPC-157 configuration is listed as research capsules in a 60-count bottle, with a listed strength of 500 mcg.
content.purpose: Laboratory study of receptor expression in rat tendon cells.
content.cautions: For nonclinical laboratory research only.

content.summary: This GHK-Cu research capsule listing specifies a 2 mg strength and a 60-capsule bottle. GHK-Cu is a copper complex studied in cell culture.
content.overview: GHK-Cu is formed by the three-amino-acid peptide glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine (GHK) and copper; the tripeptide has a high affinity for copper(II) ions. The tripeptide later identified as GHK was first reported in human serum in 1973 as a factor that prolonged the survival of normal liver cells. In a published fibroblast culture study, researchers measured collagen synthesis after exposing the cells to the complex and found stimulation beginning at picomolar concentrations and peaking near 1 nanomolar, independently of any change in cell number. Those authors noted that a GHK sequence occurs within the alpha 2 chain of type I collagen and proposed that proteases could release it at a wound site. In a rat experimental wound-chamber model, the copper complex increased wound tissue production, type I collagen and glycosaminoglycans, and it raised expression of the proteoglycan decorin in the wound tissue and in cultured rat dermal fibroblasts. These findings on the compound do not establish effects of the listed research capsules in people. This catalog configuration lists the material in capsule form for nonclinical research, in a 60-count bottle with a listed strength of 2 mg.
content.purpose: Laboratory study of collagen synthesis in cultured fibroblasts.
content.cautions: For nonclinical laboratory research only.

content.summary: The KPV research capsule listing shows a 500 mcg strength and a bottle of 60 capsules. KPV is a three-amino-acid peptide studied in cell transport experiments.
content.overview: KPV stands for lysine–proline–valine, the tripeptide corresponding to residues 11 to 13 of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH), a melanocortin peptide with described anti-inflammatory effects. One published study used intestinal and immune cell models: in the Caco2-BBE human intestinal epithelial cell line, nanomolar KPV reduced NF-kappaB and MAP kinase inflammatory signaling and lowered secretion of the cytokine IL-8, and in Jurkat T cells it reduced inflammatory signaling and IL-8 mRNA. That study examined uptake of KPV by the peptide transporter PepT1, a di- and tripeptide transporter normally expressed in the small intestine and induced in the colon during inflammatory bowel disease, and found that uptake depended on it. In mice, KPV given in drinking water reduced colitis induced by dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) or TNBS. A separate mouse study reported earlier recovery, regain of body weight and fewer inflammatory infiltrates in DSS and T-cell transfer colitis. In mice with a nonfunctional melanocortin-1 receptor, that study reported that all KPV-treated animals survived DSS colitis, and the authors concluded that the effects were at least partly independent of that receptor. These cell and mouse studies did not test a capsule formulation and do not establish effects in people. This configuration lists KPV in a 60-count bottle of research capsules, with a listed strength of 500 mcg.

content.cautions: For nonclinical laboratory research only.

content.summary: Synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide studied in rat tendon and other injury models. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide (Gly-Glu-Pro-Pro-Pro-Gly-Lys-Pro-Ala-Asp-Asp-Ala-Gly-Leu-Val) whose sequence is a partial sequence of body protection compound, a protein first isolated from human gastric juice. In cultured rat Achilles tendon explants, it accelerated the outgrowth of tendon fibroblasts. In isolated rat tendon fibroblasts, it did not directly change proliferation but improved cell survival under hydrogen peroxide stress, and it increased cell migration and spreading in a concentration-dependent way, with increased phosphorylation of the focal adhesion proteins FAK and paxillin. A follow-up study in these fibroblasts found that BPC-157 increased growth hormone receptor expression, and that adding growth hormone then increased proliferation and activated Janus kinase 2 signaling. A pharmacokinetic study measured a plasma elimination half-life of under 30 minutes for the intact peptide in rats and beagle dogs; in that study's separate experiment with tritium-labeled BPC-157 in rats, the excreted radioactivity was found mainly in urine and bile, and the authors reported that the peptide was broken down within minutes into small peptide fragments and, ultimately, single amino acids. A 2025 systematic review of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine included 35 preclinical studies and one retrospective clinical report, and reported that it found no clinical safety data in the literature it reviewed. These laboratory and animal results do not establish safety or benefit in people. The catalog lists this item at 5 mg for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Seven-amino-acid analogue of the ACTH(4-10) fragment studied in rat brain models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Semax is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide, Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, described in the literature as an analogue of the N-terminal fragment 4-10 of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). These rodent findings do not establish effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item at 10 mg for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: KISS1-derived peptide studied as the ligand of the GPR54 receptor in cell and animal models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Kisspeptins are peptides derived from the protein product of the KISS1 gene, first identified as a metastasis suppressor gene for melanoma cells, and they share a common Arg-Phe-amide (RF-amide) C-terminus. The catalog listing names this item only as kisspeptin and does not state which form it is, for example the 54-amino-acid kisspeptin-54 or the 10-amino-acid C-terminal fragment kisspeptin-10. In 2001, kisspeptins were isolated from human placenta as natural ligands of the orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR54; in hamster ovary cells expressing rat or human GPR54 they bound with low nanomolar affinity, mobilized calcium, activated ERK1/2 and p38 MAP kinases and inhibited cell proliferation. Loss-of-function mutations in GPR54 were later found to cause isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, in which pubertal maturation and reproductive function are impaired, in affected human families and in Gpr54-deficient mice. In mice, kisspeptin-54 and kisspeptin-10 delivered into a lateral brain ventricle both stimulated luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion, the kisspeptin-54 effect was blocked by a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist, and KISS1 mRNA was mapped to hypothalamic areas that regulate gonadotropin secretion. In a separate study, kisspeptin that stimulated LH and follicle-stimulating hormone release in normal mice had no effect in mice lacking GPR54, and in sheep it released GnRH into the cerebrospinal fluid, which the authors interpret as a direct action at the level of GnRH release. These cell and animal findings, and the human genetic studies of its receptor, do not establish effects of this research material in people. content.summary: Nine-amino-acid hypothalamic peptide hormone studied in receptor, lactation and social-memory research. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Oxytocin is a nine-amino-acid peptide hormone, Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2, with a disulfide bridge between its two cysteines; its gene is expressed mainly in magnocellular neurons of the hypothalamic paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei, and the peptide is released from the posterior pituitary. Its receptor is a class I G protein-coupled receptor that signals mainly through Gq proteins and phospholipase C-beta, and its classical actions are contraction of uterine smooth muscle during labor and milk ejection during lactation. Oxytocin is also made in peripheral tissues such as the uterus, placenta, corpus luteum, testis and heart, and its receptors have been found in the kidney, heart, thymus, pancreas and fat cells. Mice engineered to lack the oxytocin gene were viable and fertile and gave birth without obvious deficits, but all their pups died shortly after birth because the mothers could not nurse, and giving the mothers oxytocin after delivery restored milk ejection and rescued the pups. Male mice lacking the oxytocin gene failed to develop social memory of other mice although their detection of non-social odors and their spatial memory appeared intact, and oxytocin, but not vasopressin, restored their social memory. Synthetic oxytocin is also the active ingredient of prescription medicines used in labor and delivery; this listing is a laboratory research material, not those medicines. These animal findings, and the medical use of those separate products, do not establish the safety or effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item at 5 mg for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Nine-amino-acid peptide first isolated from rabbits and studied in EEG and sleep research. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Delta sleep-inducing peptide (DSIP) is a nine-amino-acid peptide, Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu, isolated in 1977 from the cerebral venous blood of rabbits by a research group in Basel and named for its effect on the electroencephalogram (EEG). In the original double-blind study in rabbits, synthetic DSIP infused into the brain ventricles significantly increased delta-wave and spindle EEG activity compared with controls. Of the other eight peptides tested, rabbits given one of the three shortest (two fragments and a related tripeptide) showed less significant differences from controls, and rabbits given one of the remaining five, three longer fragments and two analogues with two amino acids exchanged, did not differ significantly from controls. A 2006 review noted that this link to sleep had never been further characterized, partly because no gene, precursor protein or receptor for DSIP had been isolated by then, and that its natural occurrence and biological activity remained unclear. The same review describes the structure of DSIP as unlike any other known peptide family, and notes that DSIP-like immunoreactivity has a highly specific distribution in neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus in several vertebrate species, regions not particularly relevant to sleep regulation. The review's authors also report that certain synthetic DSIP analogues, but not DSIP itself, promoted slow-wave sleep in their own rabbit and rat studies, and they propose that a related, still unidentified peptide may account, at least in part, for the activity attributed to DSIP. These animal findings do not establish effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item at 10 mg for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Two-subunit glycoprotein hormone, described in the published record as an alpha and beta dimer and studied as recombinant subunits in cell assays. Listed at 120000 IU for laboratory research.
content.overview: Human chorionic gonadotropin, written hCG, is a glycoprotein hormone made of two different subunits rather than a single chain. A 2020 study describes hCG as a dimer of two highly glycosylated subunits, an alpha subunit and a beta subunit, and notes that the beta protein is encoded by the CGB3, CGB5, CGB7 and CGB8 genes, that CGB3, CGB5 and CGB8 encode an identical protein, and that CGB7 differs from it in three amino acids. That study produced and isolated recombinant alpha, CGB7 and CGB3/5/8 proteins and compared their glycosylation, finding the N- and O-glycosylation patterns of the two beta variants quite similar. Testing activation of the ERK1/2 pathway, it reported the two beta variants to be functionally redundant isoforms, with a slight difference in the kinetics of that activation, and recorded biological activity for CGB7 for the first time. Reference records give the alpha subunit as a 116-residue precursor with a signal region at 1 to 24 and the mature chain at 25 to 116, and the choriogonadotropin beta subunit as a 165-residue precursor with a signal region at 1 to 20 and the mature chain at 21 to 165; those records name the alpha subunit as the chain shared with the other glycoprotein hormones, so the beta subunit is what distinguishes this hormone from them. The catalog states this listing in international units, which express activity rather than mass, and no source read here states a mass equivalence for this material, so the amount is reproduced as the catalog gives it and no milligram figure is implied. This listing is a laboratory research material and not a medicine. The findings above do not establish the safety or effects of this research material in people. content.summary: Synthetic hexapeptide agonist of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, studied in pituitary cell and rodent models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: GHRP-2, also called pralmorelin, is a synthetic hexapeptide, D-Ala-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2, and by the PubChem records it is a different compound from the hexapeptide GHRP-6, whose sequence is His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. A 2004 profile of the compound describes it as a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide from a series of small, highly active peptides, and as mimicking the actions of ghrelin, the 28-amino-acid peptide, octanoylated at its third residue, that regulates the release of growth hormone. In primary cultured rat pituitary cells, antisense knockdown of the secretagogue receptor transcript reduced but did not abolish GHRP-2-induced growth hormone secretion and left the response to growth hormone-releasing hormone unaltered; knockdown of that hormone's own receptor transcript abolished its response while leaving GHRP-2's unaffected; and knocking down both inhibited both responses. In rats with thermal injury, GHRP-2 lessened the injury-induced rise in the messenger RNA of interleukin-6 and of the E3 ubiquitin ligases MuRF-1 and MAFbx in skeletal muscle and reduced total and myofibrillar protein breakdown; in mice, it produced a concentration- and time-related antinociceptive effect in a tail-immersion test that an antagonist of the secretagogue receptor fully reversed and that δ- and κ-opioid receptor antagonists markedly attenuated. content.overview: 5-Amino-1MQ is short for 5-amino-1-methylquinolinium, a small molecule from a series of methylquinolinium compounds that researchers developed to inhibit the cytosolic enzyme nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT). In one laboratory study, the team measured 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNA), a product of the NNMT reaction, in cultured mouse 3T3-L1 fat cells exposed to the compound and found concentration-dependent reductions; in differentiating cells, the compound also reduced lipid accumulation in a concentration-dependent way. In enzyme assays at the concentrations tested, it showed little or no inhibition of the related methyltransferases DNMT1, PRMT3 and COMT or of the NAD+ salvage enzymes NAMPT and SIRT1, which the authors interpreted as selectivity for NNMT. In diet-induced obese mice fed a high-fat diet, 5-amino-1MQ reduced body weight and white adipose tissue mass, decreased fat-cell size and lowered plasma total cholesterol without changing total food intake. content.summary: Nine-amino-acid peptide first isolated from rabbits and studied in EEG and sleep research. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Delta sleep-inducing peptide (DSIP) is a nine-amino-acid peptide, Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu, isolated in 1977 from the cerebral venous blood of rabbits by a research group in Basel and named for its effect on the electroencephalogram (EEG). In the original double-blind study in rabbits, synthetic DSIP infused into the brain ventricles significantly increased delta-wave and spindle EEG activity compared with controls. Of the other eight peptides tested, rabbits given one of the three shortest (two fragments and a related tripeptide) showed less significant differences from controls, and rabbits given one of the remaining five, three longer fragments and two analogues with two amino acids exchanged, did not differ significantly from controls. A 2006 review noted that this link to sleep had never been further characterized, partly because no gene, precursor protein or receptor for DSIP had been isolated by then, and that its natural occurrence and biological activity remained unclear. The same review describes the structure of DSIP as unlike any other known peptide family, and notes that DSIP-like immunoreactivity has a highly specific distribution in neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus in several vertebrate species, regions not particularly relevant to sleep regulation. The review's authors also report that certain synthetic DSIP analogues, but not DSIP itself, promoted slow-wave sleep in their own rabbit and rat studies, and they propose that a related, still unidentified peptide may account, at least in part, for the activity attributed to DSIP. content.summary: KISS1-derived peptide studied as the ligand of the GPR54 receptor in cell and animal models. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Kisspeptins are peptides derived from the protein product of the KISS1 gene, first identified as a metastasis suppressor gene for melanoma cells, and they share a common Arg-Phe-amide (RF-amide) C-terminus. content.summary: Albumin-binding analogue of GLP-1 studied in receptor assays and rodent models of body-weight regulation. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Liraglutide is an analogue of human glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in which arginine replaces lysine at position 34 and a C16 fatty acid, palmitic acid, is attached through a glutamic acid spacer to the lysine at position 26; the fatty acid binds albumin reversibly, which prolongs the peptide's presence in circulation. In the developer's 2000 report, GLP-1 derivatives carrying fatty acids of 12 or more carbons were markedly protracted compared with GLP-1, many of them with similar or higher potency at the cloned human GLP-1 receptor, derivatives with two fatty acids lost potency, and palmitate with a γ-glutamate linker was later judged the best combination of protraction and receptor potency, leading to the selection of liraglutide. Although its N-terminus is unchanged from GLP-1, liraglutide is partly protected from rapid degradation by dipeptidyl peptidase IV, which its developers attribute to reversible albumin binding or steric hindrance. In a 2014 study, liraglutide-dependent body-weight reduction in rats did not depend on GLP-1 receptors in the vagus nerve, area postrema or paraventricular nucleus; in mice, fluorescently labeled liraglutide given peripherally produced a receptor-dependent signal in circumventricular organs and in selected hypothalamic regions including the arcuate and paraventricular nuclei, with no signal in mice lacking the GLP-1 receptor; in rat hypothalamic sections, labeled liraglutide accumulated inside CART-positive arcuate cells, and in mouse brain slices GLP-1 itself depolarized pro-opiomelanocortin neurons, from which the authors propose that GLP-1 receptors on these arcuate neurons mediate liraglutide's effect on body weight. This listing is a laboratory research material and not a medicine; separately, liraglutide is the active ingredient of prescription medicines approved in the European Union in 2009 and in the United States as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus and, in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease, to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events; later approvals cover other indications for specific medicines. content.summary: Low-dose naltrexone capsules listed at 1.5 mg, far below the 50 mg naltrexone hydrochloride tablet. It is available only through the provider pathway with a prescription.
content.overview: Naltrexone is a pure opioid antagonist with no opioid agonist properties; it blocks the effects of opioids by competitive binding at opioid receptors. The FDA-approved product, naltrexone hydrochloride 50 mg tablets, is indicated for alcohol dependence and for blocking the effects of administered opioids. This capsule is listed at 1.5 mg, far below that tablet strength. A 2025 scoping review describes low-dose naltrexone (LDN) as typically 1 mg to 6 mg and states that its clinical use remains off-label, with no standardized, regulatory-approved treatment protocols. The same review identifies a need for larger clinical trials and proper dosing studies, so effectiveness for any particular condition remains under study. The indications and directions in the 50 mg tablet labeling do not transfer to this low-dose capsule. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.
content.purpose: Clinician-directed low-dose naltrexone. The 2025 scoping review cited here describes clinical use of low-dose naltrexone as off-label; the labeled indications (alcohol dependence and blockade of the effects of exogenously administered opioids) belong to the 50 mg naltrexone hydrochloride tablet labeling.
content.cautions: The FDA-approved naltrexone tablet labeling contraindicates naltrexone in people receiving opioid pain medicines, people currently dependent on opioids (including those maintained on methadone or buprenorphine), people in acute opioid withdrawal, and people with a history of sensitivity to naltrexone. content.summary: Finasteride 1 mg oral tablets, listed for clinician-directed hair-loss care through the provider pathway. Finasteride is a 5α-reductase inhibitor.
content.overview: Each tablet is listed at 1 mg of finasteride. Finasteride is a competitive and specific inhibitor of Type II 5α-reductase, the intracellular enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT). According to the PROPECIA prescribing information, blocking that conversion significantly decreases serum and tissue DHT. In men with male pattern hair loss, the balding scalp contains miniaturized hair follicles and more DHT than hairy scalp, and finasteride decreases scalp and serum DHT in these men. The FDA-approved 1 mg tablet (PROPECIA) is indicated for male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in men only; it is not indicated for use in women or in pediatric patients. Finasteride also lowers prostate-specific antigen (PSA): in PROPECIA studies of men aged 18 to 41, mean serum PSA fell from 0.7 ng/mL to 0.5 ng/mL at 12 months. A prescription is required. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.
content.purpose: Male pattern hair loss in men, the use described in FDA-approved finasteride 1 mg labeling, at the prescribing clinician's discretion.
content.cautions: Finasteride is contraindicated in women who are or may become pregnant, and the PROPECIA labeling advises that they should not handle crushed or broken tablets because absorption could harm a male fetus. It is also contraindicated with hypersensitivity to any component. The labeling notes that finasteride lowers prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels, that 5α-reductase inhibitors may increase the risk of high-grade prostate cancer, and that it is not indicated for pediatric patients. Reported adverse reactions include decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and ejaculation disorder, sexual dysfunction that continued after stopping treatment, and depression, suicidal ideation and behavior.

content.summary: Finasteride 5 mg oral tablets, a 5α-reductase inhibitor, listed for clinician-directed care through the provider pathway. A prescription is required.
content.overview: Each tablet is listed at 5 mg of finasteride, a synthetic 4-azasteroid compound. According to the PROSCAR prescribing information, the development and enlargement of the prostate gland depends on the potent androgen dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which Type II 5α-reductase produces from testosterone in the prostate gland, liver and skin. Finasteride is a competitive and specific inhibitor of Type II 5α-reductase; it slowly forms a stable complex with the enzyme that turns over extremely slowly, and it has no affinity for the androgen receptor. The FDA-approved 5 mg tablet (PROSCAR) is indicated for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men with an enlarged prostate, to improve symptoms and to reduce the risk of acute urinary retention and of surgery such as transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or prostatectomy. Combined with the alpha-blocker doxazosin, it is also indicated to reduce the risk of symptomatic progression of BPH; it is not approved for the prevention of prostate cancer, and it is not indicated for use in females or pediatric patients. In clinical studies, PROSCAR reduced serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) by approximately 50% within six months, which affects how PSA results are used in prostate cancer detection. This listing does not state the tablet's manufacturer or whether it is a brand or generic product; the dispensed product's own label governs. A prescription is required. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.

content.cautions: Finasteride is contraindicated in females who are or may potentially be pregnant, because it may cause abnormalities of the external genitalia of a male fetus, and in anyone with hypersensitivity to any component. The PROSCAR labeling states that it is not indicated for females or pediatric patients. It also states that females who are pregnant or may potentially be pregnant should not handle crushed or broken PROSCAR tablets because of possible exposure of a male fetus, that the coated tablets prevent contact with the active ingredient during normal handling if they have not been broken or crushed, and that if a pregnant female comes in contact with crushed or broken tablets, the contact area should be washed immediately with soap and water. It reports that men aged 55 and over taking finasteride 5 mg a day in a 7-year prostate cancer prevention trial had an increased risk of high-grade (Gleason score 8 to 10) prostate cancer, that finasteride lowers PSA, and that other urological conditions that may cause similar symptoms should be considered before treatment starts.

A 2026 in vitro study of human CD8-positive T cells examined its influence on their proliferation, activation, cytokine secretion and exhaustion status. content.overview: Sermorelin is a synthetic 29-amino-acid peptide amide, GRF(1-29)NH2, corresponding to residues 1 to 29 of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). content.summary: Two-subunit glycoprotein hormone, described in the published record as an alpha and beta dimer and studied as recombinant subunits in cell assays. Listed at 10,000 IU for laboratory research.
content.overview: Human chorionic gonadotropin, written hCG, is a glycoprotein hormone made of two different subunits rather than a single chain. A 2020 study describes hCG as a dimer of two highly glycosylated subunits, an alpha subunit and a beta subunit, and notes that the beta protein is encoded by the CGB3, CGB5, CGB7 and CGB8 genes, that CGB3, CGB5 and CGB8 encode an identical protein, and that CGB7 differs from it in three amino acids. Testing activation of the ERK1/2 pathway, it reported the two beta variants to be functionally redundant isoforms, with a slight difference in the kinetics of that activation, and recorded biological activity for CGB7 for the first time. Reference records give the alpha subunit as a 116-residue precursor with a signal region at 1 to 24 and the mature chain at 25 to 116, and the choriogonadotropin beta subunit as a 165-residue precursor with a signal region at 1 to 20 and the mature chain at 21 to 165; those records name the alpha subunit as the chain shared with the other glycoprotein hormones, so the beta subunit is what distinguishes this hormone from them. content.summary: 28-amino-acid thymic peptide studied in dendritic-cell and mouse immune models. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Thymosin alpha-1 is a heat-stable, highly acidic peptide of 28 amino acids, first isolated from calf thymus and sequenced in 1977. In highly susceptible mice that had received hematopoietic transplants, the synthetic peptide activated T-helper 1 antifungal immunity, accelerated myeloid cell recovery and protected against aspergillosis. content.summary: Synthetic five-amino-acid growth hormone secretagogue studied in rat and swine models. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide (Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) developed as a growth hormone secretagogue. It came from a series of compounds that lack the central Ala-Trp dipeptide of growth hormone-releasing peptide 1 (GHRP-1). In primary rat pituitary cells, anaesthetised rats and conscious swine it released growth hormone with potency and efficacy comparable to GHRP-6, and antagonist studies indicated that, like GHRP-6, it acts through a GHRP-type receptor. In swine, none of the tested secretagogues changed FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH; GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 increased ACTH and cortisol, whereas the levels after ipamorelin did not differ significantly from those after GHRH, even at more than 200 times the amount needed for half-maximal growth hormone release. In adult female rats given ipamorelin for 15 days, longitudinal bone growth and body-weight gain increased with the amount given, while total IGF-I and serum markers of bone turnover did not change. A randomized, placebo-controlled phase 2 study enrolled 117 adults undergoing bowel resection and included 114 in both its safety and modified efficacy analysis populations. The researchers described ipamorelin as a ghrelin-receptor agonist and found no statistically significant differences from placebo in the primary or secondary efficacy analyses. These cell, animal and early clinical findings do not establish that this research material is safe or effective in people. content.summary: Tadalafil 20 mg troche, a lozenge dosage form of the PDE5 inhibitor tadalafil. It is available only through the provider pathway with a prescription.
content.overview: Each troche is listed at 20 mg of tadalafil, a phosphodiesterase 5 (PDE5) inhibitor. A troche is a lozenge dosage form, different from the tablets covered by the CIALIS prescribing information cited here. According to the CIALIS prescribing information, erection during sexual stimulation comes from increased penile blood flow: nitric oxide released from nerve terminals and endothelial cells stimulates cGMP synthesis in smooth muscle cells, and cGMP relaxes that muscle so more blood flows into the corpus cavernosum. Inhibiting PDE5 enhances erectile function by increasing the amount of cGMP, and because sexual stimulation is needed to start the local release of nitric oxide, this erectile effect requires sexual stimulation. The CIALIS prescribing information describes CIALIS tablets in 5, 10 and 20 mg strengths and indicates CIALIS for erectile dysfunction, for the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia, and for both together. Those indications describe CIALIS tablets; they do not establish how this troche is absorbed or how it performs. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.
content.purpose: Clinician-directed tadalafil therapy in troche form. The labeled indications in the CIALIS prescribing information (erectile dysfunction, the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia, or both) apply to CIALIS tablets, not to this troche.
content.cautions: The CIALIS prescribing information contraindicates CIALIS with any form of organic nitrate, taken regularly or intermittently, with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat, and in people with a known serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil. It advises emergency medical attention for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, and stopping all PDE5 inhibitors and seeking medical attention after a sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes. It also warns about sudden hearing loss, additive blood-pressure lowering with alpha-blockers or other blood-pressure medicines, orthostatic symptoms with substantial alcohol (for example, 5 units or more), and interactions with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. content.summary: Sildenafil 50 mg oral tablets, a PDE5 inhibitor, listed for clinician-directed care through the provider pathway. A prescription is required.
content.overview: The catalog lists each tablet as sildenafil 50 mg. Sildenafil is a selective inhibitor of cGMP-specific phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5). According to the VIAGRA prescribing information, erection involves the release of nitric oxide in the corpus cavernosum during sexual stimulation; nitric oxide activates the enzyme guanylate cyclase, which raises cyclic GMP (cGMP), relaxing smooth muscle and allowing blood to flow in. The VIAGRA label states that sildenafil enhances the effect of nitric oxide by inhibiting PDE5, the enzyme responsible for breaking down cGMP in the corpus cavernosum, and that sildenafil at the doses it recommends for VIAGRA tablets has no effect in the absence of sexual stimulation. The labeling notes that sildenafil is only about 10-fold as potent for PDE5 as for PDE6, an enzyme in the retina, and that this lower selectivity is thought to be the basis for abnormalities related to color vision. The VIAGRA prescribing information indicates VIAGRA for the treatment of erectile dysfunction and describes its tablets as containing sildenafil citrate equivalent to 25 mg, 50 mg, or 100 mg of sildenafil. This listing does not state the tablet's manufacturer, whether it is a brand or generic product, or whether its strength is expressed as sildenafil or as the citrate salt; the dispensed product's own label governs. A prescription is required. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.
content.purpose: Labeled indication (VIAGRA prescribing information): treatment of erectile dysfunction. Whether it applies to a given patient is decided in clinician-directed review.
content.cautions: The VIAGRA prescribing information contraindicates VIAGRA with nitric oxide donors such as organic nitrates or nitrites in any form, taken regularly or intermittently, with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat, and in people with a known hypersensitivity to sildenafil or any component of the VIAGRA tablet. It notes a potential cardiac risk of sexual activity in people with preexisting cardiovascular disease, and advises stopping all PDE5 inhibitors and seeking prompt medical attention after a sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes or a sudden decrease or loss of hearing. It reports prolonged erections lasting more than 4 hours and priapism, and states that a patient with an erection that persists longer than 4 hours should seek immediate medical assistance, because priapism that is not treated immediately could result in penile tissue damage and permanent loss of potency. It also advises caution with alpha-blockers and other blood-pressure medicines, and notes that ritonavir substantially increases sildenafil levels. The VIAGRA label states that the safety and efficacy of combinations of VIAGRA with other PDE5 inhibitors, including REVATIO or other pulmonary arterial hypertension treatments containing sildenafil, or with other treatments for erectile dysfunction have not been studied. The VIAGRA label states that such combinations may further lower blood pressure and that their use is not recommended. The VIAGRA label also notes postmarketing reports of bleeding events in patients who have taken VIAGRA, and states that a causal relationship between VIAGRA and these events has not been established. It also states that VIAGRA offers no protection against sexually transmitted diseases. Share your full medication list with the prescribing clinician.

Inhibiting PDE5 enhances erectile function by increasing the amount of cGMP, and because sexual stimulation is needed to start the local release of nitric oxide, this erectile effect requires sexual stimulation. The CIALIS prescribing information describes CIALIS tablets in 5, 10 and 20 mg strengths and indicates CIALIS for erectile dysfunction (ED), for the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and for both together. Which use applies to a given patient, if any, is a clinical decision that this listing does not make. This listing does not state the tablet's manufacturer or whether it is a brand or generic product; the dispensed product's own label governs. A prescription is required. Requests go through the provider pathway, where a licensed clinician decides whether it is appropriate. Fulfillment depends on state availability and pharmacy requirements, and it is not available for direct purchase.

content.cautions: The CIALIS prescribing information contraindicates CIALIS with any form of organic nitrate, taken regularly or intermittently, with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat, and in people with a known serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil. It advises emergency medical attention for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, and stopping all PDE5 inhibitors and seeking medical attention after a sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes. It also warns about sudden hearing loss, additive blood-pressure lowering with alpha-blockers or other blood-pressure medicines, orthostatic symptoms with substantial alcohol (for example, 5 units or more), and interactions with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Share your full medication list with the prescribing clinician.

content.summary: Two-component research capsule listing stating 500 mcg of BPC-157 and 500 mcg of TB-500, described per component with no combination claim.
content.overview: This listing states two components at the strengths given in its label: BPC-157 at 500 mcg and TB-500 at 500 mcg. Each is described separately below, and no source cited here studied them together. BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide (Gly-Glu-Pro-Pro-Pro-Gly-Lys-Pro-Ala-Asp-Asp-Ala-Gly-Leu-Val) whose sequence is a partial sequence of body protection compound, a protein first isolated from human gastric juice. In cultured rat Achilles tendon explants, it accelerated the outgrowth of tendon fibroblasts. In isolated rat tendon fibroblasts, it did not directly change proliferation but improved cell survival under hydrogen peroxide stress, and it increased cell migration and spreading in a concentration-dependent way, with increased phosphorylation of the focal adhesion proteins FAK and paxillin. A follow-up study in these fibroblasts found that BPC-157 increased growth hormone receptor expression, and that adding growth hormone then increased proliferation and activated Janus kinase 2 signaling. A pharmacokinetic study measured a plasma elimination half-life of under 30 minutes for the intact peptide in rats and beagle dogs; in that study's separate experiment with tritium-labeled BPC-157 in rats, the excreted radioactivity was found mainly in urine and bile, and the authors reported that the peptide was broken down within minutes into small peptide fragments and, ultimately, single amino acids. A 2025 systematic review of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine included 35 preclinical studies and one retrospective clinical report, and reported that it found no clinical safety data in the literature it reviewed. TB-500 is a product name rather than a chemical name. A 2012 analytical study identified the peptide in TB-500 as Ac-LKKTETQ, the N-terminally acetylated 17 to 23 fragment of human thymosin beta-4, using high-performance liquid chromatography with high-resolution mass spectrometry, and prepared Ac-LKKTETQ separately by solid-phase peptide synthesis for comparison. That study examined a product sold under the name, so it establishes what the name has been shown to denote and not the composition of this listing. The seven-residue peptide is not thymosin beta-4 itself: reference records give the mature thymosin beta-4 chain as 43 residues, against the seven of this acetylated fragment, so findings reported for the 43-residue protein do not carry over to this listing. A 2015 evaluation of in vitro models for the metabolism of small peptide hormones included TB-500 among the peptides examined in human liver microsome and S9 fraction preparations. Nothing about a combination of the two is asserted. Each finding above is reported for one peptide on its own, and the properties of a combination are not established by the separate literature of its parts. This listing is a laboratory research material and not a medicine. The laboratory and animal findings above do not establish the safety or effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item as research capsules at listed strengths of 500 mcg of BPC-157 and 500 mcg of TB-500, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Synthetic six-amino-acid growth hormone-releasing peptide studied in rat and heart-tissue models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide of the growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) family, His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2, described in the literature as an analogue of GHRP-6. A 1996 rat study found that three to ten days of hexarelin pretreatment increased the later growth hormone response in 10-day-old pups, including pups immunized against GHRH, while five days of pretreatment did not enhance that response in adult males. At the tested doses, hexarelin produced the larger response in sham-operated adults; after mediobasal hypothalamus ablation, GHRH produced the larger response at seven days and the responses were similar at thirty days. Studies in infant, adult and hypothalamus-lesioned rats led its investigators to propose three mechanisms: a minor direct action on the pituitary, release of GHRH in adult animals, and release of a still unidentified hypothalamic factor. Like other GHRPs it acts on the ghrelin receptor, but in rat cardiac membranes it also binds CD36, an 84-kDa glycoprotein expressed in heart muscle cells and microvascular endothelial cells. In perfused hearts, hexarelin raised coronary perfusion pressure, and this effect was absent in hearts from CD36-null mice and from hypertensive rats genetically deficient in CD36. These rat and mouse findings do not establish effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item with a listed amount of 10 mg, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Synthetic five-amino-acid growth hormone secretagogue studied in rat and swine models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide (Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) developed as a growth hormone secretagogue. It came from a series of compounds that lack the central Ala-Trp dipeptide of growth hormone-releasing peptide 1 (GHRP-1). In primary rat pituitary cells, anaesthetised rats and conscious swine it released growth hormone with potency and efficacy comparable to GHRP-6, and antagonist studies indicated that, like GHRP-6, it acts through a GHRP-type receptor. In swine, none of the tested secretagogues changed FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH; GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 increased ACTH and cortisol, whereas the levels after ipamorelin did not differ significantly from those after GHRH, even at more than 200 times the amount needed for half-maximal growth hormone release. In adult female rats given ipamorelin for 15 days, longitudinal bone growth and body-weight gain increased with the amount given, while total IGF-I and serum markers of bone turnover did not change. A randomized, placebo-controlled phase 2 study after bowel resection enrolled 117 adults, with 114 in its safety and modified intent-to-treat populations; it described ipamorelin as a ghrelin-receptor agonist and found no statistically significant difference from placebo in its key or secondary efficacy analyses. These cell, animal and early clinical findings do not establish that this research material is safe or effective in people. The catalog lists this item with a listed amount of 10 mg, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Peptide agonist of the glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 receptors, studied in rodent models of obesity and fatty liver disease. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Retatrutide, also designated LY3437943, is a lipidated peptide of 39 amino acids designed to activate three receptors with a single molecule: the receptors for glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). In its developer's 2022 report, it showed balanced glucagon- and GLP-1-receptor activity but more GIP-receptor activity in vitro, and in obese mice it decreased body weight and improved glycemic control; the authors reported that glucagon-receptor-mediated increases in energy expenditure added to the weight loss from reduced calorie intake driven by the GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In a separate 2026 study in diet-induced obese mice used as a model of steatohepatitis, retatrutide reduced body weight, both fat and lean mass, an index of insulin resistance and liver lipid content without significantly changing energy expenditure, and in a hamster model it halved liver triglycerides without reducing liver histology scores. In a 2025 mouse model of steatohepatitis induced by a Western diet with fructose and sucrose in the drinking water, retatrutide significantly lowered body weight, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels, liver triglycerides and cholesterol, and hepatic inflammatory markers in female mice compared with vehicle controls. In isolated mouse atria, retatrutide did not increase the force of contraction of the left atrium but raised the beating rate of the right atrium, an effect antagonized by a glucagon-receptor antagonist. As of a review covering evidence through September 2026, retatrutide was an investigational medicine in phase 3 clinical development and was not approved; this listing is a laboratory research material, not a medicine. These laboratory and animal findings do not establish the safety or effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item at 10 mg of retatrutide, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Synthetic seven-amino-acid tuftsin analogue studied in rodent models of GABAergic signaling. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) designed as an analogue of the endogenous peptide tuftsin. The selected studies examine GABA-related signaling, gene expression and behavior in rodent and tissue models. In brain membrane binding assays, Selank changed [3H]GABA binding in a way consistent with positive allosteric modulation of GABA receptors, and it blocked the modulatory effect of diazepam and olanzapine on that binding. In the rat frontal cortex, Selank altered the expression of many of 84 neurotransmission-related genes at one and three hours; the one-hour changes correlated positively with those produced by GABA, and the three-hour changes correlated negatively. In mouse spleen, Selank and its C-terminal Gly-Pro fragment changed the expression of immune-related genes such as complement C3 within 30 to 90 minutes, with similar profiles for both peptides. In rats given ethanol as their only fluid for 30 weeks, Selank prevented memory and attention deficits during withdrawal and prevented the ethanol-related rise in BDNF in the hippocampus and frontal cortex. These findings come from rodent and tissue studies and do not establish effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item with a listed amount of 10 mg, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: 29-amino-acid active fragment of human GHRH studied in pituitary cell and rat models. Listed at 5 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Sermorelin is a synthetic 29-amino-acid peptide amide, GRF(1-29)NH2, corresponding to residues 1 to 29 of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). A 1999 review describes it as the shortest synthetic peptide with the full biological activity of GHRH, acting specifically on the anterior pituitary to stimulate growth hormone secretion. In rat anterior pituitary cells in culture, the 1-29 amide fragment of human GHRH retained about half the potency of the full-length peptide. In the same study, shorter amidated fragments down to residues 1-21 still released growth hormone with full intrinsic activity at much lower potency, and activity disappeared only at residues 1-19. In rats, the growth hormone response to GRF(1-29) was markedly reduced in hypothyroid animals, which the authors interpreted as altered responsiveness of the pituitary somatotroph cells. This listing is a laboratory research material and not a medicine; separately, sermorelin has been studied clinically, including as a diagnostic test of pituitary growth hormone secretion. These cell and animal findings do not establish effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item with a listed amount of 5 mg, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: Stabilized analogue of human growth hormone-releasing factor studied in pig, rat and dog models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Tesamorelin, developed under the code TH9507, is an analogue of the 44-amino-acid human growth hormone-releasing factor, hGRF(1-44)NH2, modified only by a trans-3-hexenoyl group added to the N-terminal tyrosine. That modification made it resistant to inactivation by dipeptidyl aminopeptidase IV and slowed its breakdown in rat, dog and human plasma in vitro. In vivo, the investigators reported longer plasma persistence for immunoreactive TH9507 than for the natural peptide. In dogs, the apparent elimination half-life of that immunoreactive signal was 21 to 45 minutes. In pigs, rats and dogs, repeated administration markedly increased plasma growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). In subchronic studies of up to four months, rats and dogs gained more body weight, and dogs showed reversible liver, kidney and blood findings that the authors attributed to sustained supraphysiological growth hormone and IGF-1 exposure. This listing is a laboratory research material and not a medicine; separately, tesamorelin is the active ingredient of a prescription medicine approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in November 2010 for an HIV-related indication. The animal findings above, and the approval of that separate medicine, do not establish the safety or effects of this research material in people. The catalog lists this item with a listed amount of 10 mg, for nonclinical laboratory research.

content.summary: 28-amino-acid thymic peptide studied in dendritic-cell and mouse immune models. Listed at 10 mg for laboratory research.
content.overview: Thymosin alpha-1 is a heat-stable, highly acidic peptide of 28 amino acids, first isolated from calf thymus and sequenced in 1977. It corresponds to the N-terminal region of the larger precursor protein prothymosin alpha. It was one of several polypeptides in the thymic extract thymosin fraction 5 proposed to take part in the differentiation and function of T cells. In dendritic cells exposed to the fungus Aspergillus fumigatus, thymosin alpha-1 induced functional maturation and interleukin-12 production through MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor signaling involving p38 MAP kinase and NF-kappaB. In highly susceptible mice that had received hematopoietic transplants, the synthetic peptide activated T-helper 1 antifungal immunity, accelerated myeloid cell recovery and protected against aspergillosis. This listing is a laboratory research material, not a medicinal product. A separate literature review discusses clinical studies of thymosin alpha-1. The dendritic-cell and transplant findings above come from cell and mouse studies and do not establish effects of this research material in people.
